messages:
Priya K: incident-bot just paged me — single-tenant Dedicated pool for customer `OrchidHealth` is showing sustained GPU queueing and evictions. app p95 latency spiking, customer facing timeouts. :warning:
incident-bot: [AUTOMATED] Alert: pool=dedicated-orchid-1 metric=gpu.queue_length value=312 threshold=200 first_seen=3189989960
Priya K: Observed: 4/8 GPUs at 98% util, queue depth 300+, pending requests climbing. Autoscaler not reacting — suspect scale-inhibit from pinned capacity or scheduled maintenance.
Alex R: oncall here, taking this. any impact to other tenants?
Priya K: early signs show token generation failures are from Orchid's tenant lane only (requests routed to their reserved slice). Other tenants are nominal but we have spillback enabled so some Orchid requests are queuing on shared routing which is adding latency.
Jamie S: tagging infra — can we force burst from the shared burst bucket while we triage? policy allows emergency burst for enterprise customers with managed contracts, but need approval from Carlos (acct).
Carlos M: I'm awake — Orchid is on a committed monthly plan with burst credits up to 120 GPU-min. approve emergency burst to avoid customer SLA breach. confirm duration and estimate cost.
Alex R: estimate: to drain queue need ~30 GPU-min extra over 20 minutes at current qps. recommending 30 minutes to be safe. propose command: `rbctl pool burst --pool dedicated-orchid-1 --gpus 2 --duration 30m --reason "incident: queueing"`
Priya K: quick mitigation plan: 1) enable burst (if Carlos OK) 2) reduce Orchid concurrency from 8->4 via rate-limit override, 3) failover long-tail jobs to smaller quantized model (gpt-small-8q) to lower token compute.
Jamie S: how confident about model swap? risk of quality regression but acceptable short-term. need routing rule change: set model_fallback=quantized-small for tenant Orchid for 30m.
Alex R: I'll run the commands and monitor. Priya can you push the rate-limit change? I'll request burst from infra.
sre-rotation: Alex, if you apply burst, remember to tag with incident id and set auto-revoke. use `--auto-revoke 35m`. also add a billing tag.
Alex R: running burst now. exec log: ```
$ rbctl pool burst --pool dedicated-orchid-1 --gpus 2 --duration 30m --auto-revoke 35m --tags incident=orchid-3189990001 billing=emergency
Burst request submitted: id=burst-8f7a, state=PENDING
```
incident-bot: [SYSTEM] Burst request burst-8f7a APPROVED by billing policy; allocation active on nodes g4-42,g4-43.
Priya K: applying tenant concurrency cap: ```
PATCH /v1/tenants/orchid/config
{ "rate_limit": { "concurrency": 4 }
}
```
Priya K: routing override applied: model_fallback -> gpt-small-8q for tenant Orchid. logs show a drop in avg GPU latency immediately.
Alex R: after burst active, queue depth dropped from 312 -> 48 within ~90s. GPU util dropped to ~80%. p95 latency back to normal range for most requests. putting customer status update in progress.
Carlos M: confirming cost: burst used ~28 GPU-min so far. billing will invoice against burst credits then overage. good to proceed with auto-revoke at 35m.
Jamie S: note for postmortem: why autoscaler didn't kick — possible causes: pinned capacity flag, scale policy cooldown, or a bug in the scale controller when dedicated pools are pinned. assigning to eng-runtime to investigate.
Alex R: handing off to oncall-eng-runtime — @Jamie S and @Priya K will coordinate follow-up. marking incident status: mitigation=achieved, owner=Alex R, next_steps=investigate autoscaler root cause, customer postmortem, update runbook.
Priya K: I've posted a customer-facing note to Orchid support channel: "We've applied temporary burst and throttling to stabilize your service — engineering is investigating root cause. We'll follow up with timeline."
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] Status changed -> MONITORING by Alex R at 3189990150
Alex R: leaving notes: - no cross-tenant eviction observed - prefer targeted rate-limit + model fallback next time over full pool throttle - document the command sequence used.
Jamie S: adding runbook todo: - validate autoscaler behavior when pool is pinned - add synthetic to detect queueing earlier (queue length synthetic alert at 100) - create a safe rollback plan for model fallback.
sre-rotation: acknowledged handoff. I'll escalate to eng-runtime oncall for a postmortem. tagging this thread for later. :thumbsup:
Carlos M: customer logged as Sev2, billing informed. good job all.
Alex R: closing live triage. last checks show stable. will keep monitoring until auto-revoke. if anything flares reopen thread.
Priya K: thanks team. adding incident notes to the tracker. :heart:
